rules: 1. Main tables keep the locked local seed-0 row. Nothing is re-based on a seed mean.

2. Every named claim is retested with each seed: the three tuned-minus-stock gains; tuned LFM vs stock Qwen3 0.6B and vs stock Jina 1.5B under the level rule; here-minus-elsewhere too if the seed adapters get scored on the other repos.
3. A claim is written without qualification only if all three seeds agree. Otherwise the sentence gives the seed mean, its interval, and how many seeds meet the rule.
4. Watched claim: 'tuned LFM is level with stock Jina 1.5B' (lower bound -.046 against the -.05 margin).
5. If seeds exist for Saleor only, the test runs on Saleor's per-repo difference, and the paper says so.

6. No mixed GPUs in the seed table: where a same-seed 4090 rerun exists, the seed spread comes from the three 4090 runs (Jina .729/.719/.724) and the local row is printed next to it. Main-table rows are labelled single local runs. For Jina on Saleor, the local run is the highest of the four.

config.rule: Split of the first run by search use. For each of B, C and D: gold-file rate of that arm and of arm A, paired difference with interval, on (i) issues where that arm called search at least once and (ii) issues where it did not. For D only: on its search issues, how many had the gold file in the search results. Reading rule: (1) If D − A is +.03 or more on the no-search issues and below +.15 on the search issues, the gain is there without a search call; the sentence 'we do not credit the difference to search' stands and cites the cell. (2) If D − A is below +.02 on the no-search issues and +.15 or more on the search issues, the gain sits where search was called; the sentence changes to report that as an observational lead, with its confounds. (3) Anything else: the text prints both cells and reads nothing into them. Caveats logged with the rule: the first run's search-use breakdown was already reported before this rule was logged (2026-11-12), so this rule is not blind; and the split conditions on something the agent chose.

extra.timing: logged before this request's cells were computed or read
extra.analyst_disclosure: Stronger than the logged caveat: the D-by-search-use split (D - A gold file on D's search and no-search issues, with intervals, same bootstrap) was already computed as a cell of scripts/cc-analysis.py (its cache, not shipped) and had been seen before this rule was written, so the analyst knows which case of this rule D falls in. The B and C splits against A were not computed before; their with/without-search gold-file rates (not paired against A) were reported.
